conservation_statuses.description: Sorbus torminalis is a tree found across the much of southern, western and central Europe. It is here assessed as Least Concern for Europe and the EU 28 member states as it covers a huge area of Europe. Subpopulations can be small and isolated so it may be necessary to protect populations in some countries. This species is threatened, like other Sorbus by changes in forest management and grazing as well as a fungal disease.

results.wikipedia_summary: Torminalis is a genus of plants in the rose family, Rosaceae. The genus was formerly included within the genus Sorbus as the section Torminaria, but the simple-leafed species traditionally classified in Sorbus are now considered to form a separate monophyletic group. It is monotypic, being represented by the single species Torminalis glaberrima, commonly known as wild service tree, chequers, and checker tree. This tree is native to Europe, parts of northern Africa and western Asia.
